build: Decibel and Eagle Soft Incorporated side A, Eagle Soft Incorporated side B

exclude: Neighbouring byte left by the disk intro. The selector reaches the high nibble of $FFF8 and leaves the cursor on that byte before returning to its menu.
extra: The Lotus colour decoder reads the surviving intro byte beyond the end of _1
GP module relocated to $29BC from the side B catalogue
DP module relocated to $2C3B from the side B catalogue

comments.text: Relocated entry $29C0 followed by the $027B-byte GP body length.
Look up the bitmap resource named by $38–$39, set the bitmap base from $34, and read the traversal flag and nine escape tokens. A resource ID of $FFFF jumps into the colour path.

Read literal bytes and repeat records through $2AA1. Escape index zero supplies its own count, while the other indices determine the count. Advance the bitmap destination through $2A5B after each output byte.
Advance the bitmap position after a decoded byte. The flag read from the bitmap sets the order of columns and scanlines.
Read the next packed bitmap byte through an absolute operand patched with the resource pointer and advance that operand.
Resolve the colour resource, read its rectangle header and initialize the colour escape table. Feed decoded values and runs to $2B78 until the writer signals that the rectangle is complete.
Zero the column, row and plane counters in $7E, $7F and $7D.
Read two packed nibbles and combine them into one explicit repeat count by patching the immediate OR operand.
Read through $04–$05, return the high nibble first, then the low nibble. Advance the pointer after the low nibble.
Reset the nibble phase, read ten colour escapes beginning at offset seven, then advance the source pointer 17 bytes to the packed colour stream.
Write the decoded colour value into the current section of the rectangle and advance the destination. The placement and size derive from the loaded colour header.
Zero byte after the return at $2BF3 and before the 25-entry row-offset low table that begins at $2BF5.
Low bytes of 25 screen row offsets at forty bytes per row. The colour writer reads this at $2B9A.
High bytes of the same row offsets, added to the base page of the selected screen or colour plane at $2BA1.
Complementary high- and low-nibble bit masks between the row-offset high table and the bitmap compositor opcode table.
The two GP opcodes are BIT zero page and EOR indirect indexed. GP patches the bitmap writer with one of them to select direct storage or an exclusive-OR merge.
Nibble values shifted left by four bits. The second screen pass preserves the low nibble of the destination and uses this table for the new high nibble.
Relocated entry $2C3F followed by the $0225-byte DP body length.
Take a mode byte from the caller stack. Bit 1 requests a four-page copy using the high bytes in $36 and $37. Bit 0 chooses between the bitmap merge and mask-only paths.
Visit the first bitmap using the page and byte permutations at $2D32 and $2D52. Mask each byte and merge it into the corresponding byte of the second bitmap.
Visit the pages of the second bitmap in permuted order and clear selected bits through the mask table at $2E5B.
Zero byte between the mask pass return and the start of the page permutation table.
Permutation of the 32 bitmap page indices. The two loops at $2C8B and $2CEF OR each entry with a bitmap bank high byte.
Permutation of the 256 offsets within a bitmap page. The loops at $2C84 and $2CE8 use the selected value as their byte index.
Mask table indexed by the pass counter in the source bitmap merge at $2CA3.
Mask table for the destination-only pass. The AND at $2CFF uses the current pass index.
Relocated entry $2E68 and body length $0144 for CI.
Executable entry returns immediately. The selector reads the relocated address words following this byte as data.
Tagged address records used through the CI base at $06-$07. The code selects one of five three-byte records at $30B5, then uses two six-byte-per-car groups for the bitmap lists at $3163 and $325F.
Bytes addressed by the final descriptor at $2EB4. The selector reads car-specific pairs using the pointer loaded at $31DA.

Five groups of selected asset suffixes. The selector's loop skips zero entries and exits on $FF. Each group contains the car-specific short attribute and bitmap lists referenced by the preceding address records.
Relocated entry $2FB0 and body length $0713 for TS.
Reset the input latch, install the temporary IRQ, locate the graphic and car descriptions, and initialize selection to car zero.
Derive the disk item suffix from the selection at $40 plus ASCII '1'. Invoke GP and DP to prepare the selected car and wait for selector input.
Check the confirmation latch at $46, otherwise use the joystick index at $E2 and the table at $36B1. Advance or decrement $40 and wrap within five entries.
Stop the selector music through $6400 and release the car-select assets. Read the selected car's records through the module base $06 before preparing the driving display.
Copy 32 pages between the bitmap buffers selected by $34 and $35. Invoke the graphics loader and look up the car-specific assets by the selected car's suffix.
Immediate delay input to $350E. Its value comes from the second byte of the selected car's pair at $31F3.
Load the first specification transition resource ID for index $DE. A zero ID ends this transition list.
Low byte of the list address used by $3204. The selector patches it at $31C4 from the CI record selected by $40.
High byte of the indexed load at $3204, patched from the CI table by $31CA.
Load the second specification transition resource ID for the same index, then pass it to the colour overlay lookup.
Low byte of the list address used by $3211. The selector patches it at $31D1 from the same CI record.

High byte of the indexed load at $3211. The CI table supplies the target at $31D7. The remaining loop temporarily adjusts each colour resource's vertical origin for the GP blit and restores it afterward.
Wait until $42 is below ten, then choose the next pitch step and reset the transition's resource cursor.
Compute the selected car's CI record index and patch the two absolute loads at $32A8 and $32B2.
Use the timing table at $364E to choose the next bitmap band. Draw the pair of resources at the current list index, then request a display update.
Read the first resource ID for this transition frame. Zero resets the list index to zero before trying again.
Low byte of the list address used by $32A8. The store at $3267 takes it from the selected car record.
High operand byte of $32A8, populated from the selected CI record before its first lookup.
Load the paired transition resource ID at the index that supplied the first ID at $32A8.
Low byte of the paired list address, written at $3274 before the transition loop.
High operand byte of $32B2, from the second pointer in the same record.
Synchronize the $D418 writes with the counter at $30 and lower the volume from 12 to zero.
Opcode-tagged address of the IRQ entry at $3361. $333A and $3340 read the address bytes.
Low byte of the first selector IRQ vector. Startup copies it to $0314 at $2FB8.
High byte of the alternate selector IRQ vector, installed at $3343.
Acknowledge the VIC interrupt and advance $30. Process pending bank and scroll changes, latch fire, check the keyboard and service music before resuming the KERNAL IRQ.
If requested by $32, combine the upper bits of $D016 with the pending scroll value at $33. Test for port 2 fire before restoring the port and leaving the interrupt.
Absolute-load opcode byte before the two-byte IRQ vector at $33C9. The setup at $300D reads the vector starting one byte later.
Low byte of the second selector IRQ vector. Setup writes it to $0314 at $3010.
High byte of the second selector IRQ vector. Setup writes it to $0315 at $3016.
Enable I/O, acknowledge the VIC-II interrupt, select the next raster phase and update horizontal scroll. At phase zero, service bank changes, selector joystick input and music.
Find the active-low direction nibble in the table at $36BA and put its index in $E2. OR an active fire button into the confirmation latch at $46.
Patched to JSR during transition sound and restored to BIT after the fade. The operand targets the second gate at $349C.
A BIT instruction ordinarily skips the resident call at $0842. The transition patches its opcode to JSR while the effect is active.
Advance the pitch accumulator and clamp it to the bounds checked at $34AF and $34BF before writing the scaled frequency to SID voice 1. Preserve the caller's $04 pointer.
If the keyboard queue contains M, invert the flag at $5A.
Add A to the running IRQ tick at $30 and wait for that value.
Supply scanline bounds $78 and $C8 to the alternate entry into the bitmap copier.
Work with the selected offset and the visible bitmap addresses computed from the row and column tables.
Set the display request at $31 from A and spin until the IRQ clears it.
Resolve the resource with the module lookup, read dimensions and position from its six-byte header, apply the current animation offsets, then draw the bitmap at the selected bank.
Invoke the resident service at $0824 with Y equal to $F2.
Call UJ with the selected two-byte asset ID on the stack, then free the reusable graphic item identified by the self-modifying operands at $3647 and $3649.
Immediate at $3646, patched with the first original archive ID byte before calling UJ.
Immediate at $3648, patched with the second original archive ID byte for the tail call to $0806.
Zero byte immediately before the transition band increments. The indexed load at $3283 starts at $364E.
Values added to the fine scroll residue by $3288. A zero ends the band animation and enters the volume fade.
Map the eight possible low scroll bits to the value written into $33 before the display request.
Low bytes of row times 40, used by the matrix-copy loop at $3575.
High bytes paired with $3677. The copy combines them with the screen page.
Two next-phase values indexed by $DD. The IRQ at $33E9 alternates the phase between one and zero.
Per-phase bits ORed with $36AF,X and sent to VIC-II $D016 at $33E0.
Two raster compare values sent to $D012 at $33E6.
Per-phase bits combined with $36AB,X at $33DD. The transition handler updates the first byte at $33FF.
Indexed by the direction result from $E2. Zero leaves the current car and the signed entries advance or decrement the selection.
Nine active-low direction patterns read by the input loop at $3470.
